snapshot.text: Air France-KLM, a network airline in the European peer group, ended FY2025 with a stronger credit profile as revenue rose by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} and EBITDA by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}}.

Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}} and gross leverage by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}, with the EBITDA margin widening by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}.

The main point to watch is liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, the weakest of the network peers ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@2025}}), while capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}.

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, the weakest of the network peers ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@2025}}), with cash and cash-like investments flat at {{cash_like@FY2025}}.

Investment: capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@2025}}, which keeps free cash flow thin at {{fcf@FY2025}} and FCF to debt at {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}, the weakest of the group ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@2025}}).

Debt: total debt rose by {{total_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{total_debt@FY2025}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{net_debt@FY2025}}, so the lower net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2025}} rests on EBITDA holding at {{ebitda@FY2025}}.

Customer prepayments: contract liabilities of {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}} rose by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}}, and advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is below the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@2025}}, a sensitivity if bookings slow.
